validity.recommendation: Existence, classification, and twin-line structure confirmed; no action needed on these points.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/DUPLICATE: P6036 ('Pipeline 2') and its sibling P5132 ('Pipeline 1') are NOT a double-count of one pipe. Multiple independent trade sources confirm Zohr field is served by (at least) two physical 30-inch export trunklines to the El-Gamil onshore treatment plant near Port Said: the original line that came online with first commercial gas in Dec 2017, and a second 30-inch line added later as production ramped up (nsenergybusiness.com/offshore-technology.com describe 'Zohr I' and 'Zohr II', each ~216km; Offshore Magazine independently reports 'a new 30-in., 218-km pipeline, commissioned [Aug 2018]' tied to the T4 production-unit startup; Rigzone reports a Saipem contract addendum for a second 30-in export pipeline as part of the 'Ramp Up to Plateau' phase awarded ~Jan 2019). GEM's two-row model (Pipeline 1 / Pipeline 2 under one wiki page) is a reasonable way to represent this twin-line reality, not a duplicate. One nsenergybusiness passage even states the project includes 'three gas export pipelines, including two 30-inch pipelines' (Saipem's own project page mentions a '26-inch gas export trunkline' too) -- there may be a third physical line GEM hasn't captured, but that is a Discovery-workflow question, out of scope for this row-level audit; flagging for awareness only. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk (major offshore field-to-shore export line feeding the national grid via El-Gamil), not a gathering/process/plant-internal line -- confirmed. Sources used: nsenergybusiness.com/projects/zohr-gas-field-mediterranean-sea/, offshore-technology.com/marketdata/zohr-i-gas-pipeline-egypt/, offshore-technology.com/marketdata/zohr-ii-gas-pipeline-egypt/, offshore-mag.com/.../zohr-building-to-peak-gas-offshore-egypt, rigzone.com/.../offshore_egypt_project_to_start_new_phase-20-dec-2018-157768-article, ogj.com/.../zohr-pipeline-component-installation-offers-custom-deepwater-guidance, saipem.com/en/saipem-worldwide-projects/gas-field-offshore-zohr. Current status also independently reconfirmed as active/operating into 2025-2026 (Zohr field still producing ~2.7-3.2 bcfd, new wells being brought online in 2025-2026 per egyptoil-gas.com and ecofinagency.com), even though the sheet's current Status [ref] (nsenergybusiness) technically failed the automated 'operating' string check.

validity.recommendation: Replace Owner1-4 (Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co 48%, Eni SpA 26%, Naturgy 13%, SEGAS 13%) with the actual Zohr/Shorouk-concession ownership: Eni 50%, Rosneft 30%, BP 10%, Mubadala (Petroleum/Energy) 10%, operated by Petrobel (Eni/EGPC 50:50 JV). This should be checked/fixed on P5132 too if it carries the same owner block.
validity.researcher_notes: The current Owner block on this row (Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co 48%, Eni SpA 26%, Naturgy 13%, SEGAS 13%) does not match the Zohr field/pipeline ownership under any independently sourced structure I could find, and the specific names 'Naturgy' + 'SEGAS' + 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' are unmistakably the ownership of a DIFFERENT asset -- the SEGAS Damietta LNG liquefaction plant (Spanish Egyptian Gas Company), not the Zohr upstream/export-pipeline concession. Eni press releases (verified) confirm SEGAS's actual ownership history: pre-2021 it was 80% Union Fenosa Gas (= 50% Eni + 50% Naturgy, i.e. 40%/40% of SEGAS) + 10% EGAS + 10% EGPC; post-restructuring (closed March 2021) it became Eni 50% / EGAS 40% / EGPC 10%. Neither matches the sheet's 48/26/13/13 split either, so this looks like a garbled/miskeyed copy of Damietta-LNG ownership data into the Zohr pipeline row, not the real Petroshorouk concession partners. The actual, independently and repeatedly confirmed Shorouk-concession/Zohr partners are Eni 50%, Rosneft 30% (since Oct 2017 stake sale), BP 10%, Mubadala Petroleum/Energy 10% (since June 2018 stake sale) -- field/pipeline OPERATOR is Petrobel (Belayim Petroleum Co), a 50:50 Eni/EGPC joint venture, distinct from the ownership percentages. This is a high-confidence attribution error given the SEGAS/Naturgy names are specific and non-generic.

validity.recommendation: Re-verify LengthKnown; independent sources consistently give ~216-218km for BOTH Zohr export lines, not 210.00km. Recommend correcting to ~216km unless a source specific to 'the second line at 210km' can be found (none located).
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's LengthKnown for this row is 210.00km. Every independent source found (nsenergybusiness.com and its sister offshore-technology.com [GlobalData/NS Media family, so treated as one source-family] AND the fully separate Offshore Magazine/Endeavor Business Media) states BOTH Zohr export pipelines are ~216km (GlobalData family) or 218km (Offshore Magazine, describing the 'new 30-in., 218-km pipeline commissioned' for the second line specifically). None of the sources found distinguish a 210km figure for either line. This is a ~3% but consistent discrepancy against two source families; not corroborating GEM's exact value. GulfPub (Tier-2, this project's registered reference dataset) models the Zohr export system very differently -- as short subsea tie-ins (~80km 'Zohr Gas Export Pipeline'/'Pipeline II', Zohr field to Denise field) plus a separate 'Denise - Port Said Pipeline' (46km) -- which doesn't map cleanly onto either the 210 or 216/218km figures, so it does not resolve the discrepancy and was not used to adjudicate it.

validity.recommendation: Cross-check StartYear1 against sibling P5132: the 2017/2019 values on the two rows appear to be transposed relative to independent chronology (the FIRST line started Dec 2017; the SECOND, later-added 30in line started ~2018-2019). If 'Pipeline 2' is meant to be the later-added line, its StartYear1 should likely be ~2018/2019, not 2017 -- but if GEM's 'Pipeline 1'/'Pipeline 2' labels don't track build order, no change may be needed. Recommend a human check of both rows together; do not change unilaterally.
validity.researcher_notes: This row (labeled 'Pipeline 2') carries StartYear1=2017, while sibling P5132 (labeled 'Pipeline 1') carries StartYear1=2019. Independent sources are clear that Zohr's ORIGINAL/first 30in export line began commercial operation in December 2017 (widely and repeatedly corroborated -- Eni's own Dec 2017 press release, nsenergybusiness, offshore-technology 'Zohr I'), and a SECOND 30in line was added later: Offshore Magazine reports a 'new 30-in., 218-km pipeline, commissioned [Aug 2018]' tied to the T4 production unit; Rigzone/OGJ describe a further Saipem EPCI contract addendum ('Ramp Up to Plateau' phase) for another 30in export pipeline awarded ~Jan 2019; offshore-technology's 'Zohr II' page states operations began in 2019. So 2017 is a genuine, well-sourced start year for ONE of the two physical lines -- it is just ambiguous (and, given the 'Pipeline 2' label, possibly backwards) whether it belongs to THIS row or to P5132. I could not find any source that names 'Pipeline 1' vs 'Pipeline 2' as GEM defines them, so I can't independently confirm which row should carry which year -- flagging for a human pass across both rows rather than silently reassigning.

fills.researcher_notes: Zohr is Egypt's largest gas field discovery; this is unambiguously a natural gas export pipeline. Fuel=Gas confirmed.
Both export pipelines carry Zohr field gas to shore; confirmed by multiple independent sources.

Start (Shorouk concession, offshore Mediterranean) and end (Port Said / El-Gamil onshore treatment plant) endpoints are corroborated: nsenergybusiness names the Shorouk block and El-Gamil terminal explicitly; Saipem's own project page confirms subsea pipelines terminating at 'ground handling facilities in Port Said'. nsenergybusiness/offshore-technology share a publisher (GlobalData/NS Media) so marked independent=false at the pair level, but Saipem is a fully separate, first-party corroborating source for the Port Said endpoint. Tier set to medium given the primary named-endpoint source (El-Gamil specifically) rests on one publisher family.

routes.start_name: Zohr field / Shorouk concession, offshore Mediterranean Sea (~190km N/NNW of Port Said, water depth ~1,450-1,700m)
routes.end_name: El-Gamil (Al-Gameel) onshore gas treatment plant, Port Said governorate
routes.corridor_desc: Subsea trunkline running roughly south from the Zohr field location within the Shorouk block (Egypt's offshore EEZ, Mediterranean Sea, ~190km from Port Said per nsenergybusiness/offshore-technology, in deepwater up to ~1,700m per Saipem) to the El-Gamil/Al-Gameel onshore gas treatment plant just west of Port Said city, Port Said governorate, where it ties into the national grid. I could not source precise lat/lon for either endpoint from an independent (non-GEM) source: a WebSearch snippet surfaced coordinates for the Zohr field from a page it attributed to Global Energy Monitor itself (unusable -- circular) and a separate snippet cited a wikimapia stub giving El-Gamil plant coordinates (~31.306N, 32.155E) but the live page returned only a ~150-char stub on fetch, so I could not verify that figure directly and am not using it. Both endpoints are therefore given as named places only, coordinates null, per the no-fabrication rule. The corridor is tightly bounded at the onshore end (Port Said governorate, El-Gamil specifically) and loosely bounded offshore (Shorouk block generally, ~190km N/NNW of Port Said) -- not tight enough to support more than 'low' suggested accuracy without a sourced map or well coordinates.
routes.researcher_notes: Named endpoints are solid (Shorouk/Zohr field offshore -> El-Gamil onshore, Port Said) but no independently-sourced coordinates were found for either end, so accuracy cannot be upgraded past low without further map/technical-paper research. Did not fabricate coordinates; left null per instructions.

summary: P6036 is a real, correctly-classified twin export line of the Zohr field (confirmed, not a duplicate of sibling P5132) but has a likely wrong Owner block (looks like miskeyed SEGAS/Damietta-LNG ownership instead of the real Eni/Rosneft/BP/Mubadala Shorouk-concession split), a Length (210km) that independent sources put closer to 216-218km, and a StartYear (2017) that may be transposed with P5132's 2019 -- all staged as concerns, not applied.
